question: How can one of the biggest hits of its year show no profit at all?
answer: On paper, easily. When a columnist sued Paramount over the 1988 hit Coming to America, the studio's accounts showed no net profit, because distribution fees, overhead charges and interest came off first. A Los Angeles court found parts of that formula unconscionable in 1990. Writers learned to ask for a share of the gross instead.
move: A share of profit is worth only what the one counting defines as profit.
reference: O'Donnell and McDougal, Fatal Subtraction, Doubleday, 1992
